Root check -x test failed (BUILD FAILED in 3m 46s) at :solr:core:forbiddenApisTest, and a standalone rerun of that task reproduced it (rc=1). Seven forbidden class/interface uses, all in org.apache.solr.update.StreamingSolrClientsErrorAttributionTest at lines 159, 160, 163, 164 and 171: org.apache.logging.log4j.core.LogEvent and org.apache.logging.log4j.message.Message, each flagged 'Use slf4j classes instead'. Mechanism: the review-fix commit added a log-assertion block that drains LogListener queues; the queue element type is log4j's LogEvent, so the test class's calls to getMessage() and getThrown() reference the banned types. The prior head's test file contains no log-capture block (verified by direct comparison), so the violation is introduced by the gated commit itself, in test code only; no production class is flagged. The UI wasm artifact for the check was seeded by curl with its SHA-256 matching the build pin (654494303e4af3b8bfb26a83d250603f19033820295591d88db0597991ce8ad2), the established remedy for this host's egress relay corrupting that download; the check failure is unrelated to it.

Connection refused', meaning the prior head's per-request error log events still carry the stream's exception where the fixed behavior carries none. Not a compilation, setup or unrelated failure.
